probe_dims: one branch, one object type with 12 properties, one link type, one action type, one dataset write from CSV
result: documented: creates and updates object, link and action types on a branch; creates Python transforms repositories; writes datasets from CSV; reads build and job status; creates egress policies; clones repositories locally and opens pull requests; connects a non-Foundry Git repository to a Developer Console application. Documented NOT to write ontology data, and no tool listed for AIP Logic, AIP Evals, Workshop, Pipeline Builder or Solution Designer. This is the fallback landing route if SuperRepo is unavailable, and the primary route for the seven pipeline nodes either way. Confirm against the installed version, not the docs page.

probe_dims: one screen using useOsdkObjects, one using useOsdkFunction, one using useOsdkAction
result: carried evidence from a parallel build, unconfirmed here: the data hooks call useSyncExternalStore with no getServerSnapshot, so renderToString throws for any data-bound screen. Pin the limitation with an asserting test so it goes red the day the library ships the capability.

probe_dims: one query publishing an optional nullable string parameter documented as omittable
result: carried evidence from a parallel build, unconfirmed here: the hook's params type wraps the query's in NotOptionalParams, so the React binding cannot express an absent optional parameter without a cast. The mismatch is in the binding, not in the function.

probe_dims: clean install of the generated SDK after moving one function import forward one minor version
result: carried evidence from a parallel build, unconfirmed here: the generated client continued to emit the older function version after the import list moved, silently, with no error and no warning. Import list and invoked version are decoupled.

probe_dims: one repository at this build's template version, dependency manifest and verifyPackageJson task
result: carried evidence from a parallel build, unconfirmed here: the template mandates @osdk/language-models and @palantir/functions-sources and the build fails when either is absent; not overridable through build.gradle, gradle.properties or functions.json. This is why the determinism assertion is reachability from entry points rather than absence from the repository.

probe_dims: one global branch, one functions repository, one ontology import, one query registration
result: carried evidence from a parallel build, unconfirmed here: a functions-typescript-v2 repository could not join a global branch; ontology imports had to be on the default branch; a query with an apiName could not be registered from a repository with no ontology imports. These shape which node can be built on a branch at all.

probe_dims: one list of 6 required elements, each with a constrained select, a one-line justification field and 2 evidence links
result: no prior evidence. Buy-before-build candidate for the one repeated component. If ObjectTable cannot host a constrained select plus a free-text justification per row, the prebuilt path costs more than it saves.

probe_dims: all of 7 CFR Part 1b, §§ 1b.1 to 1b.12, retrieved twice in separate processes
result: no prior evidence at this build. Establish whether a structured API exists before writing a parser, and whether two retrievals of the same effective version are byte-identical.

probe_dims: the amendment lineage of 7 CFR Part 1b plus the final-rule preamble
result: no prior evidence at this build. Establish rate limit, page size and whether the preamble is retrievable as text.

probe_dims: the USDA/USFS slice only, not the whole corpus
result: no prior evidence at this build. Establish row grain (document or chunk), whether page-level text exists, and the selectivity of a USDA/USFS filter. Download size at full corpus is a build risk in itself.

probe_dims: the v1.2 crosswalk CSV at a pinned commit
result: no prior evidence at this build. Establish (entity, property) uniqueness and how many PIC entities have no counterpart in this build's shape.

probe_dims: one trivial external call to one public endpoint
result: no prior evidence at this build. If egress is unavailable, every source is downloadable and bulk upload is the path; the build proceeds unaffected. Do not spend a session fighting the network.

probe_dims: three USFS documents, one of them scanned, one with a chunk straddling a page break; plus one document carrying a list-of-preparers section, to measure named-role extraction yield
result: no prior evidence at this build. Page anchoring is what makes the citation check work, so per-page extraction is the requirement rather than the method; establish whether it is available and whether it returns page numbers.

probe_dims: one justification slot, ten invocations, two separate processes, fixed sampling
result: no prior evidence at this build. The drafter's MR-4 requires identical grounding_kind and identical canonical_path set across processes; establish whether fixed sampling delivers that, because prose variance is acceptable and binding variance is not.

probe_dims: one drafter, ten cases, binding-resolution and value-match reported as two rows
result: no prior evidence at this build. Palantir MCP lists no AIP Evals tool, so establish whether an evaluation suite can be defined and its results written to a dataset by anything an agent can drive, or whether the measurement loop is hand-configured.

probe_dims: one SuperRepo via `foundry create`; one object type declared in Ontology-as-code and one imported from the UI; one TypeScript v2 function; one React screen calling it; embedded Ontology preview run locally; one `foundry deploy` to the training enrollment
result: Beta as of the week of 2026-08-03 and MAY NOT BE AVAILABLE ON THIS ENROLLMENT — probe availability first, before anything else. A SuperRepo is a monorepo holding Ontology-as-code (object types, links, interfaces, actions declared in TypeScript), TypeScript v2 functions, and the React application, developed locally through the Foundry CLI with an embedded Ontology preview, and compiling natively into a signed Marketplace product. Code definitions are the source of truth and materialize as real entities on deployment; types created in the UI can be imported into code and vice versa. NOT yet supported and confirmed in Palantir's own roadmap page: Python functions, data pipeline support, Automate, an agent SDK, and external source support for SuperRepo functions. The last two bind n.drafter directly.
